description: This bar chart illustrates five distinct patterns of parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces, each represented by a horizontal bar plot with five bars per group. The horizontal axis serves as the category axis, displaying the five labeled patterns — “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck” — from left to right. The vertical axis represents the magnitude or value of the design space metric, though its specific label, scale type (linear or logarithmic), and units are not provided. The value range of the vertical axis is not explicitly stated, but the bars are visually scaled to represent relative magnitudes within each group. Each group of five bars shows a different distribution: the “Increasing” pattern shows bars progressively increasing in height from left to right; the “Uniform” pattern shows all five bars of equal height; the “Decreasing” pattern shows bars progressively decreasing in height from left to right; the “Spindle” pattern shows two tall bars in the middle with shorter bars on either side; and the “Bottleneck” pattern shows two tall bars at the ends with shorter bars in the middle. The bars are rendered in a uniform light gray color without additional visual emphasis such as shading, bolding, or annotations. The chart does not indicate whether the bars are sorted in any specific order beyond their categorical grouping, and no legend is present to explain what each bar represents.
